articles.headline_en: Controversy over abortion fees: SDP MP deletes social-media post criticising the government
articles.significance: The case concerns a Finnish opposition politician removing a post after criticism over claims about abortion-related fees, illustrating how political disputes can lead to the deletion of social-media content.
articles.summary_en: Finnish media reported that an SDP member of parliament deleted a social-media post criticising the government in a dispute over abortion-client fees. The National Coalition Party accused the opposition of spreading false information about the fees.

articles.headline_en: NGO asks the European Parliament to investigate the Greens over antisemitism
articles.significance: The complaint raises questions about the responsibility of politicians and political parties for hateful or extremist comments posted by third parties on their social-media pages.
articles.summary_en: An NGO asked the European Parliament to investigate German Green politicians over comments posted on their social-media pages. The complaint alleges that account holders failed to remove posts praising Adolf Hitler, collectively blaming Jews for conflict in the Middle East, or describing Israelis as monsters.

articles.headline_en: Giorgia Meloni’s ‘UN speech’ goes viral in an altered video despite the Italian prime minister not attending the assembly
articles.significance: The incident shows how manipulated online political content can falsely attribute controversial statements to a serving European leader and spread through social media.
articles.source: International Business Times UK — United Kingdom
articles.summary_en: A viral altered video falsely portrayed Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni delivering a speech at the 2026 UN General Assembly and announcing a sanctions policy. The report found no evidence that Meloni attended the assembly or made the statements attributed to her.

articles.headline_en: The lucrative business of reactionary AI-generated posts on Facebook
articles.significance: The report highlights the growth of coordinated political-content networks that violate platform rules involving inauthentic behaviour, impersonation, spam and misinformation.
articles.summary_en: Le Monde examined networks producing reactionary AI-generated content for Facebook. The networks reportedly operate in coordination and systematically breach platform policies on inauthentic behaviour, impersonation, spam, misinformation and engagement baiting.

articles.headline_en: Veran Matić: Everyone is against KRIK
articles.significance: The article discusses concerns in Serbia that proposed changes to public-order legislation could restrict speech and revive forms of censorship associated with the country’s socialist past.
articles.summary_en: The report said Serbia’s Protector of Citizens, Zoran Pašalić, had announced changes to the Law on Public Order and Peace. Critics feared the changes could amount to a return of the ‘verbal offence’ and censorship of spoken expression formerly associated with Yugoslavia.

editorial_overview: Coverage during the week focused on several forms of pressure surrounding political speech online: deletion of a politician’s post, complaints about moderation on politicians’ pages, manipulated videos falsely attributed to leaders, and coordinated AI-generated political content. The reports also reflected broader concerns about state or institutional restrictions on expression, particularly in Serbia. The available coverage did not establish a single Europe-wide policy shift, but it showed continuing tension between political communication, platform moderation, misinformation and free-expression protections.
topic: European press review: political speech, social-media removals and digital censorship — 18–25 September 2026
